## Scope and audience

This self-paced course supports people who need a practical introduction to accelerometer workflows, including:

- undergraduate and graduate students in kinesiology, public health, epidemiology, data science, and related fields;
- research assistants, coordinators, laboratory staff, and investigators;
- faculty and instructors using the course for methods teaching or team onboarding;
- public-health, clinical, exercise, and human-movement professionals;
- data analysts and methodologists; and
- company and consulting teams working in wearable technology, digital health, occupational health, research services, or related fields.

The concept route is suitable for beginners and requires only a web browser. The hands-on route also requires an approved or fictional protocol, safe practice data, and access to the relevant software or devices. The course covers device placement and programming, file organization, GGIR quality review and processing, and preparation of a participant-level dataset.

The course is educational guidance, not a substitute for a study protocol, statistical analysis plan, local data-governance requirements, or device-manufacturer instructions.

## Stewardship and review status

- **Course steward:** LA PASSSTA Lab, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
- **Current course version:** 1.3.0
- **Content review date:** August 11, 2026
- **Technical baseline:** GGIR 3.3-7 documentation
- **Video-version note:** the Module 4 demonstration was recorded using GGIR 3.3-6; the lesson text identifies decisions that should be checked against the version installed for a new study
- **Published video quality:** all ten course videos are delivered from 1920 × 1080 masters; technical corrections and the removal of production-only material are retained in the published versions

Software interfaces and defaults can change. Before production analysis, consult the [current GGIR parameter documentation](https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html) and record the package version and complete configuration used for the study.

## AI-assisted video transparency

The course videos use AI-assisted production and narration. English captions and readable transcripts were generated from the media and corrected against the course terminology. They are provided for review and accessibility, but they may not reproduce every spoken hesitation or visual-only detail. Please [report a caption or content error](https://github.com/uiuclapasssta/accelerometer-learning-course/issues) with the module name and timestamp.

## Accessibility

The site is designed to support keyboard navigation, visible focus, responsive text and controls, descriptive headings, captioned videos, readable transcripts, and reduced-motion preferences. We aim to improve toward WCAG 2.2 Level AA; this statement is not a certification of full conformance.

Known limitations:

- Some instructional details appear visually inside recorded software demonstrations and may not all be described in the audio.
- Downloaded R and Stata files require compatible software or a plain-text editor.
- Third-party documentation linked from the course has its own accessibility practices.

For an accessibility problem, [open an issue](https://github.com/uiuclapasssta/accelerometer-learning-course/issues) and describe the page, device, browser, and assistive technology if you are comfortable doing so.

## Privacy

Course information remains publicly readable without identifying yourself. A learner who chooses to sign in and accepts the learning-data notice can create a synchronized course record containing the entry questionnaire, module activity and completion, submitted quiz attempts and answers, course feedback, and certificate status. A random internal learner ID links those records; the display name is not used as an authentication credential. Browser storage remains a resilience cache, not the authoritative record for a signed-in learner.

The course does not use these records for UIUC grades, academic assessment, or an official UIUC credential. Access is restricted to the learner and designated course administrators. Review the complete [learning-data privacy notice](data-privacy.qmd) before opting in. It explains the fields collected, purposes, retention period, access, export and deletion controls, and certificate verification behavior.

If you arrive through the former course address and choose to copy saved progress, the migration bridge transfers only recognized course records directly between the two browser windows. The saved values are not placed in the URL or submitted to the course team, and the former-site copy is retained.

The public pages remain static GitHub Pages content. Authentication, authorization, authoritative scoring, completion checks, and certificate issuance are performed by the separate course data service; browser controls are never treated as security boundaries. Enter only your own information and never enter participant, health, confidential, or other sensitive information.

GitHub hosts the public pages and [states that it logs and stores a visitor's IP address for security purposes](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages#data-collection), whether or not the visitor is signed in. That hosting record is separate from the course learning record.

Links to GitHub and external documentation are governed by those services' own privacy practices.

## Certificate of completion

Learners who complete the entry questionnaire, mark all eight modules complete, pass the final knowledge check, and save the required final feedback can create a personalized certificate of completion.

The certificate uses Illinois-inspired color and formal typography and can be printed or saved as a PDF from the completion page. For an opted-in learner, the course service verifies the requirements and issues a high-entropy verification code. Anyone given that code can check the displayed learner name, course version, issue date, and current certificate status on the verification page.

## Rights, reuse, and citation

No explicit open-source license is attached to the course at this time. Unless a file states otherwise, copyright remains with LA PASSSTA Lab and the relevant contributors or rights holders. Contact the course steward before redistributing or adapting substantial course content.

Suggested citation:

> LA PASSSTA Lab. *Accelerometer Learning Course*. Version 1.3.0. University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, 2026. https://uiuclapasssta.github.io/accelerometer-learning-course/

Use the repository's [GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/uiuclapasssta/accelerometer-learning-course/issues) for technical errors, broken resources, accessibility problems, or suggested clarifications. Do not include participant data, protected health information, credentials, or other sensitive material in a public issue.
